newsitem.title: FRANCE: National Front candidate wounded in French town.
newsitem.headline: National Front candidate wounded in French town.

text.p: An extreme rightist candidate in a bitterly-contested muncipal election in this southern French town was badly beaten up by unidentified men, police said on Friday.

Gilles Lacroix of Jean-Marie Le Pen's National Front (FN) party, known for its anti-immigrant stance, was in hospital after being sprayed in the face with tear gas before being beaten and left unconscious in the street, police said.

The local FN branch blamed the town of Vitrolle's outgoing Socialist administration of provoking the incident with verbal attacks against the rightists but police said nothing proved Socialists were involved.
The election, in which a mainline centre-right candidate is also taking part, has drawn nationwide attention since the head of the FN is the wife of Bruno Megret, national deputy head of the FN.
Megret himself was ineligible after a court found he overspent the maximum sum allowed in an election during a prior vote in 1995. He has been closely involved in his wife's campaign.
The Vitrolles vote is also seen as a test of FN strength after it captured three key southern France muncipalities, including that of the southern port of Toulon in elections two years ago.
